scope: Foundational reconstruction of patient and population health observation, disease and injury boundaries, diagnosis, causal clinical inference, prognosis, intervention, exposure, benefit-harm, study designs, care pathways, individual-population inference, consent, privacy and uncertainty.
exclusions: living mechanism already owned by Biology is cited rather than rederived
molecular identity and reaction law already owned by Chemistry are cited rather than rederived
device and biomaterial law already owned by Materials is cited rather than rederived
specialty-by-specialty complete-field reconstruction belongs to later Medicine versions
institutional policy is not treated as a biological or clinical law
future medical discoveries remain lawful extensions after independent admission

obligations.title: Patient identity
obligations.statement: A patient is one consent-bound person carrier whose episode records may compose only while their exact linkage, context and provenance remain held.

obligations.title: Clinical episode
obligations.statement: A clinical episode is a finite ordered patient trace with explicit entry, observations, actions, exit and retained follow-up boundary.

obligations.title: Clinical population
obligations.statement: A clinical population is a finite set of retained person carriers selected by declared criteria, never an average that erases membership or source frame.

obligations.title: Health state
obligations.statement: A health state is a context- and time-bound organization of retained functional, experiential and survival distinctions rather than an unqualified single label.

obligations.title: Clinical observation
obligations.statement: A clinical observation binds the observed carrier to observer, method, setting, time and result so the observation cannot silently become the law.

obligations.title: Longitudinal clinical course
obligations.statement: A longitudinal course is an ordered within-person state relation that preserves every observed interval, missing visit, intervention and censoring event.

obligations.title: Normal clinical variation
obligations.statement: Normal variation is the observed support within a declared reference population and method; it is not a universal numerical threshold.

obligations.title: Dysfunction boundary
obligations.statement: Dysfunction requires a retained functional relation, baseline, context and consequence and cannot be inferred from difference alone.

obligations.title: Disease state
obligations.statement: A disease state is a criteria-bound harmful process whose mechanism, manifestations and course remain distinct; a label alone is not the state.

obligations.title: Injury state
obligations.statement: An injury binds a declared exposure to damage and consequence at a retained site, time, severity and observation method.

obligations.title: Comorbidity composition
obligations.statement: Comorbidity is a joint condition word on one patient and interval; component conditions and their interactions may not be collapsed into one label.

obligations.title: Severity and stage
obligations.statement: Severity and stage are declared finite order relations over retained criteria and may not be silently treated as interchangeable or universal scales.

obligations.title: Symptom record
obligations.statement: A symptom is a patient-reported observation whose content, timing, context, elicitation and reporting uncertainty remain held.

obligations.title: Clinical sign
obligations.statement: A sign is an observer-elicited feature with method, observer, setting and time retained; it is not interchangeable with a symptom.

obligations.title: Clinical measurement
obligations.statement: A clinical measurement retains carrier, unit, method, calibration, preanalytic state, result, uncertainty and reporting transformation.

obligations.title: Diagnostic classification
obligations.statement: Diagnostic classification maps a complete patient evidence word to a declared class while retaining alternative classes, criteria and verification boundary.

obligations.title: Differential diagnosis
obligations.statement: A differential diagnosis is a retained finite support of candidate conditions reduced only by recorded patient evidence; an untested alternative may not disappear.

obligations.title: Diagnostic accuracy
obligations.statement: Diagnostic accuracy requires all four cells generated by held condition and test-result distinctions plus population spectrum, reference method and verification record.

obligations.title: Clinical association
obligations.statement: A clinical association is an exact joint-incidence relation at a declared population and interval and does not by itself assert cause.

obligations.title: Clinical causal claim
obligations.statement: A clinical causal claim requires a lawful contrast with timing, exchangeability boundary, intervention or counterfactual meaning and complete outcome follow-up.

obligations.title: Clinical mechanism
obligations.statement: A clinical mechanism is an ordered, independently observed chain connecting exposure to outcome; a plausible biological name alone cannot close it.

obligations.title: Clinical confounding
obligations.statement: Confounding is retained whenever a pre-exposure cause bears on both exposure and outcome; adjustment must state exactly which distinctions it conditions on.

obligations.title: Clinical mediation
obligations.statement: Mediation separates direct and mediator-carried paths only when their temporal and intervention meanings are explicitly generated and observed.

obligations.title: Clinical effect modification
obligations.statement: Effect modification is a retained variation of a treatment or exposure contrast across predeclared strata on a declared comparison scale.

obligations.title: Clinical risk
obligations.statement: Risk is an exact outcome share among an explicitly eligible at-risk set over a declared positive finite horizon, with competing events and loss retained.

obligations.title: Incidence and prevalence
obligations.statement: Incidence counts new condition transitions while prevalence counts supported states; the two observation relations may not be merged.

obligations.title: Clinical prognosis
obligations.statement: Prognosis is the exact support of future outcomes conditional on a complete baseline and care context, never an unqualified fate label.

obligations.title: Clinical outcome
obligations.statement: A clinical outcome retains endpoint definition, baseline, assessment time, method, assessor and every component or adverse alternative.

obligations.title: Censoring and competing events
obligations.statement: Censoring and competing events are explicit course outcomes; neither may be silently treated as absence of the target event.

obligations.title: Prognostic calibration
obligations.statement: Calibration compares predeclared risk groups with every observed outcome row in a distinct population and interval without post-outcome retuning.

obligations.title: Clinical intervention
obligations.statement: An intervention is a completely specified patient-directed action whose content, delivery, adherence, context and timing remain recorded.

obligations.title: Clinical comparator
obligations.statement: A comparator is an explicit alternative action evaluated under the same eligibility, outcome and time boundary; omitted care is not numerical zero.

obligations.title: Clinical counterfactual
obligations.statement: A counterfactual denotes alternative courses for the same eligibility state; because only one course is observed, the missing course and identification boundary must remain explicit.

obligations.title: Intervention allocation
obligations.statement: Allocation is a fully traced deterministic assignment sequence whose concealment can prevent selection even though SFT imports no ontological nondeterminism.

obligations.title: Adherence and crossover
obligations.statement: Adherence and crossover preserve assignment, received care, timing and reason as distinct labels rather than rewriting the allocated history.

obligations.title: Clinical cointervention
obligations.statement: Every concurrent care action that can change an outcome remains in the intervention word and may not be hidden inside an arm label.

obligations.title: Dose
obligations.statement: Dose is an exact positive finite relation among amount, recipient carrier, formulation, route and schedule; no universal effect follows from dose alone.

obligations.title: Clinical exposure
obligations.statement: Exposure retains source, path, route, intensity, duration, person and measurement or reconstruction method.

obligations.title: Clinical response
obligations.statement: A response is a recorded change from baseline after an exposure or intervention, with controls required before the temporal relation becomes causal.

obligations.title: Dose-response relation
obligations.statement: A dose-response relation retains every administered dose group, outcome, route, interval and nonmonotone or adverse pattern; no fitted curve is the law.

obligations.title: Adverse event
obligations.statement: Every unfavorable event after care remains recorded with seriousness, severity, timing, relatedness assessment and final outcome, whether or not causally attributed.

obligations.title: Clinical toxicity
obligations.statement: Toxicity requires an exposure-linked harmful transition with dose, organ or function, timing, recovery and alternative causes retained.

obligations.title: Efficacy
obligations.statement: Efficacy is a complete intervention-comparator outcome contrast under declared explanatory trial conditions.

obligations.title: Effectiveness
obligations.statement: Effectiveness is the corresponding contrast under retained real-care delivery, adherence, population and setting variation.

obligations.title: Safety evidence
obligations.statement: Safety is a complete comparative adverse-outcome record at a declared exposure and follow-up boundary, never proof that harm is absent.

obligations.title: Benefit-harm composition
obligations.statement: Benefit and harm remain separate outcome components and may compose only under an explicit population, horizon and value boundary.

obligations.title: Absolute and relative effects
obligations.statement: Absolute and relative effects are distinct exact readings of the same complete arm-by-outcome table; neither may replace the underlying counts.

obligations.title: Treatment-effect heterogeneity
obligations.statement: Treatment heterogeneity requires the complete joint stratum, arm and outcome support with predeclared comparisons and multiplicity retained.

obligations.title: Clinical trial
obligations.statement: A trial is a prospective finite process retaining protocol, eligibility, allocation, arm flow, outcomes, deviations and all analyses.

obligations.title: Randomized allocation in a deterministic model
obligations.statement: Randomization is a reproducible held-label allocation process whose future labels are concealed from selectors; it imports no nondeterministic ontology.

obligations.title: Clinical blinding
obligations.statement: Blinding is an exact information-access restriction by role and stage with every planned or accidental unblinding event retained.

obligations.title: Observational clinical study
obligations.statement: An observational study retains source population, sampling, exposure, outcomes, confounders, missingness and follow-up and does not silently become an intervention.

obligations.title: Clinical evidence synthesis
obligations.statement: Evidence synthesis composes purpose-matched study carriers while retaining design differences, dependence, heterogeneity, bias, adverse and absent results.

obligations.title: Missing and selective reporting
obligations.statement: A registered outcome or study absent from the visible report remains an explicit missing distinction and cannot be interpreted as a favorable absence.

obligations.title: Screening
obligations.statement: Screening is the whole test-to-confirmation-to-care pathway in a declared asymptomatic population, including false results, overdiagnosis and downstream harms.

obligations.title: Prevention
obligations.statement: Prevention is an action preceding a declared outcome in an at-risk carrier, with prevention level, comparator and all later outcomes retained.

obligations.title: Treatment
obligations.statement: Treatment binds a declared indication to delivered therapeutic action, comparator, response, harm and follow-up rather than to intent alone.

obligations.title: Rehabilitation
obligations.statement: Rehabilitation is an iterated, goal-bound relation among intervention, function, participation and lived context across retained timepoints.

obligations.title: Clinical monitoring
obligations.statement: Monitoring is a predeclared sequence of measurements and action rules; the measurement history may not be replaced by the latest value.

obligations.title: Stopping and withdrawal
obligations.statement: Stopping or withdrawal is a recorded care transition with reason, alternative, taper or aftercare and post-transition outcomes held.

obligations.title: Individual clinical inference
obligations.statement: Individual inference conditions only on the available patient evidence and preserves unsupported alternatives, values, context and uncertainty.

obligations.title: Population clinical inference
obligations.statement: Population inference requires an explicit sample-to-source relation with selection, missingness, eligibility, place and time retained.

obligations.title: Clinical transportability
obligations.statement: Transportability requires explicit source-target comparison and may carry only relations invariant under every retained population and setting difference.

obligations.title: Subgroups and multiplicity
obligations.statement: Every generated subgroup and outcome comparison remains in one complete family so selection after outcomes cannot masquerade as prior inference.

obligations.title: Clinical decision boundary
obligations.statement: A clinical decision composes evidence with explicit actions, consequences and patient values; a population average cannot uniquely select an individual action.

obligations.title: Clinical uncertainty
obligations.statement: Clinical uncertainty is the exact retained support after available evidence, including known missingness and unresolved alternatives, not an ontological nondeterminism claim.

obligations.title: Informed consent boundary
obligations.statement: A consent record is valid only for its declared person, information, understanding, voluntariness, purpose, scope and time, with refusal and withdrawal retained.

obligations.title: Decision capacity boundary
obligations.statement: Capacity is decision- and time-specific evidence over retained abilities and assistance; diagnosis or status alone cannot erase the person's choice.

obligations.title: Clinical privacy
obligations.statement: Clinical privacy requires purpose-bound access, minimized disclosure and a complete identity-content-recipient-time trace; public evidence may not expose an unnecessary person link.

obligations.title: Clinical data minimization
obligations.statement: A clinical dataset may retain only fields forced by its declared purpose while preserving an auditable record of exclusion, derivation, access and retention.

obligations.title: Clinical equipoise and stopping boundary
obligations.statement: A comparative study remains admissible only while its declared evidence support leaves the care alternatives unresolved and its harm-stopping rules remain active.

obligations.title: Clinical evidence handoff
obligations.statement: A medical claim may cross to a reviewer only with reconstructible derivation, data provenance, code, adverse/null/unresolved rows, privacy boundary and custody record.
